extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers interested in Garry Shandling or television/comedy history
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia article summarizing Garry Shandling's life, career, notable works, style, and influence in comedy and television. Serves as a reference for readers researching his persona, shows, and contributions to the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: Clean comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Infobox lists Shandling's style as 'Clean comedy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a preference for humor that avoids explicit/obscene content; used as a concise label of his comedic approach. (No further elaboration on the page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking the fourth wall / meta-sitcom format
rubrics_metrics.description: “The series subverted the standard sitcom format by having its characters openly acknowledge that they were all part of a television series... incorporated the audience and elements of the studio into the storylines, calling attention to the show's artifice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a deliberate production choice for It's Garry Shandling's Show, rooted in earlier precedents (e.g., George Burns). Guidance: use overt meta-commentary and studio/audience elements to call attention to artifice; this is an example of a successful formal innovation credited on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic persona: anxiety-ridden, nervous, uptight character
rubrics_metrics.description: “Shandling's onstage persona was an anxiety-ridden, nervous, uptight, conservative man on the verge of a breakdown.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents this persona as central to his stand-up identity and material — using vulnerability and neurosis as comedic fuel. Implied guidance: a distinctive, consistent persona can be a core comedic tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal experience as material
rubrics_metrics.description: Shandling turned real-life events (e.g., a near-death car crash and its aftermath) into part of his routine and creative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article treats mining personal life events as a legitimate and effective source of material for comedy and storytelling; example: his accident inspired career decisions and became routine material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic performance: 'eliminating the acting' to 'be'
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing acting coach Roy London and DVD testimonies: Shandling insisted on eliminating the 'acting' from the 'being' and having performers 'just be' — working on life and acting simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as a creative/directorial principle underlying Shandling's shows: favoring authenticity and naturalistic performances over obvious 'acting'. Used as guidance for directing actors and shaping performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock behind-the-scenes talk-show satire (grounded in real experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Larry Sanders Show is described as a 'mock behind-the-scenes talk show sitcom' based on Shandling's experiences guest-hosting The Tonight Show — a format that yielded critical and commercial success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criteria for this kind of satire: grounding the mockumentary/behind-the-scenes conceit in lived experience and workplace detail enhances authenticity and critical reception. The page notes influence on later shows (Entourage, 30 Rock, Curb Your Enthusiasm) as evidence of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator involvement: writing/directing as a quality marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Shandling wrote many episodes of his series (15 for It's Garry Shandling's Show; 38 for The Larry Sanders Show) and directed episodes; his hands-on role is repeatedly noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents heavy creator involvement (writing, producing, directing) as correlated with the shows' distinctiveness and acclaim. Awards/nominations for writing and producing are cited as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations as indicators of success
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists extensive recognition: e.g., nominations for 19 Primetime Emmy Awards (19 total during his career), Emmy wins, Golden Globe nominations, CableACE awards, BAFTA, American Comedy Awards, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used on the page to signal critical/industry validation — number and prestige of awards are presented as metrics for a show's or performer's impact and success.
